subtype: Approach: using a coloured chart pinned on the wall [Action]
passage:
Hrithik: Didi, why is the wall covered in colours?
Amandeep: It's my week chart. Blue is maths, green is science, orange is Hindi, pink is drawing.
Hrithik: Tuesday is nearly all green!
Amandeep: Science and its practical file are both on Tuesday. First I ruled the days, then I coloured the boxes, then Papa helped me pin it up. Now I glance once and I know which books go in.
Hrithik: Can I make one, chhote bhai style?
Amandeep: You are the chhote bhai. Take the markers. What do you colour first?
Hrithik: Sports, in red!
Amandeep: Good. Yours goes lower on the wall, where you can reach.

qa.q: Which colour stands for science on Amandeep's chart?
What does Hrithik seem to want when Hrithik asks to make a chart too?
qa.a: Hrithik wants a chart like Amandeep's; the eager questions and choosing red for sports show real interest.

qa.q: What other approach could help Hrithik get the bag right, and why?
qa.a: Hrithik could read the timetable in the evening and pack the night before, because a calm check at home means fewer mistakes in the morning. A short list at the door could also work.

qa.q: How might Papa see the colour chart on the wall?
qa.a: Papa probably sees a sensible habit; Papa helped pin it up and is likely happy for both children to have one.

grounding: A girl colours each subject on a weekly chart pinned on the wall so the day's books are clear at a glance.

subtype: Approach: using a coloured chart pinned on the wall [Action]
passage: In Class 6 I kept carrying the wrong books, so one Sunday I made a chart. I drew a big grid on chart paper: Monday to Saturday across the top, periods down the side. Then I gave each subject a colour: Maths blue, Science green, Hindi orange, English red. I coloured every box and pinned the chart on the wall right above my study table. That night, packing for Tuesday, I just looked for the colours: two blues, one green, one red. Done in a minute. My little brother Kashish said, 'Madhuri didi, it looks like a rainbow exploded.' Maybe. But I haven't carried a wrong book since.

qa.q: What colour did Madhuri give Maths?
How did Madhuri feel about packing once the chart was up?
qa.a: Madhuri felt relieved and pleased, since packing for Tuesday took only a minute of spotting colours 😊

qa.q: What could Madhuri do if a subject moves to a different day?
qa.a: Recolour that box or stick a note on it, so the chart stays true; the colours work because she can read a day at a glance.

qa.q: How does Kashish see the chart?
qa.a: Kashish teases that it looks like a rainbow exploded, so to him it seems funny and a bit much.

grounding: Shows a girl making a colour-coded weekly timetable chart by her study table so she can see which books belong to each day.

subtype: Approach: using a coloured chart pinned on the wall [Action]
passage: Class teacher's note, 7C, for the parents' meeting. Ayesha used to come without the right books two or three times a week. After the first term she showed me something she had made at home: a weekly chart where every subject had its own colour, pinned by her study table. She brought a photo of it. Now, she told me, she just matches colours when she packs. I've checked her bag on random days this month: every book right. Kashish, who sits beside her, has started a chart too, in felt pens. I'll suggest it to the whole class on Monday.

qa.q: How often did Ayesha use to come without the right books?
qa.a: Two or three times a week.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt showing the photo of her chart?
qa.a: She was probably proud and pleased to share something she made that fixed her problem.

qa.q: What could make the chart idea work for the whole class?
qa.a: Each student making a colour chart and pinning it where they pack, as Ayesha did, and updating it when the timetable changes.

qa.q: How does the note-writer see Ayesha's chart?
qa.a: The note-writer checked her bag on random days, found every book right, and plans to suggest the idea to the class.

grounding: Illustrates a girl's colour-coded weekly chart by her study table helping her pack the right books, as seen by her teacher.
